    <h1>Team assignments</h1>

{% raw %}
Alagos keeps **standing teams** for Gotham: every player has a job (City Hall, a cannon team, or Reserves) and keeps it week after week. The weekly team post shows those same jobs, so nobody has to relearn their place. The Ultimate (UBG) and Battle for Gotham (BfG) teams are kept separately; every `/teams` command takes `type:` and defaults to Ultimate. This needs **Post team assignments** (officers by default).

## Setting the teams by hand

On every plan, **✏️ Assign players** on `/teams show` sets jobs by hand:

1. Pick a job: **City Hall**, **Cannon Team A** to **F**, or **Reserves**.
2. Open a range of names. Each opens a list of checkboxes, already ticked for whoever holds that job; anyone else shows where they are now.
3. Tick someone to move them into the job from wherever they were. Untick them to take them off it, and they are "not on a team yet".

Players who hold a job but are **inactive** or **on leave** are in the lists too, marked, so you can untick them.

On the **Free** plan this is how the teams are made: nothing is built or placed for you, and until some teams are set there is no team post. On **Premium** it is the quick way to fix a few people without a rebuild.

## Building the teams automatically (Premium)

Run `/teams setup`. It shows a **preview** built from your active roster (anyone on leave is left out), balanced on recent Gotham attendance. Nothing changes until you press **✅ Create these assignments**.

Running it again later rebuilds **everyone**: the preview says how many people would move and suggests `/teams drift` instead. Pinned players never move.

## The weekly team post

In the event editor, a Gotham event's **Notifications** tab has a **Team Post** time. At that time the teams are posted in the event's channel, pinging its mention role. Setting it on one week carries over to the following weeks. Post it the day before if your league relays the teams in game.

The post never moves anyone. On **Premium** it places **newcomers** (active players with no job yet) where there is room, and lists anyone it could not place. A seat held by an **inactive** player counts as room, so City Hall is filled first; someone **on leave** keeps their seat until they are back. On **Free** nobody is placed for you: players with no job are listed under **🙋 Not on a team yet**, so they know to ask and you can see who is left. Signups do not change the standing teams.

Under the post:

- **📋 Copy for in-game mail**: the teams as plain text, names only, ready to paste into in-game mail. Officers only.
- **🔄 Rebuild**: redraws the post with the latest roster (for example after placing someone). It does not reshuffle anyone.

## Looking after the teams

`/teams show` lists the current teams, each cannon team's total power and how far apart they are, who is pinned, who is not on a team yet, and who holds a job but is inactive or on leave.

- **🧹 Remove inactive players** (shown when someone inactive still holds a job) lists them and, once you confirm, takes only them off their jobs, pinned or not. Nobody else moves, and players on leave keep their jobs.
- **🩹 Fill the gaps** (Premium, shown when a seat can be filled) refills empty seats with as few moves as possible, and shows the moves before anything changes:
  - a **City Hall** seat takes the strongest player in **Reserves** who qualifies (inside the power range, if City Hall uses one); if nobody in Reserves does, the strongest cannon player who qualifies moves up;
  - a **cannon team** with a set size takes the strongest player left in Reserves;
  - with nobody in Reserves the seat stays empty: it never pulls someone off another team, which would only move the gap;
  - pinned players and the ERT are never moved.
- **📌 Pin a player** keeps someone in their job through every rebuild and drift suggestion. Unpin them from the menu.
- **Start over** removes every standing job (it asks first). On Premium, posts are then built from scratch each week until you run `/teams setup` again; on Free there is no post until you assign players again.

## Drift: who has outgrown their job (Premium)

Players get stronger. `/teams drift` shows cannon players who now outrank City Hall members, paired with the City Hall member they would swap with.

A swap is only suggested once the gap has lasted: the player must outrank at least a few City Hall members (**Drift Threshold**, default 3) for a number of weeks (**Drift Patience**, default 3), both on the **DC Dark Legion** tab of `/guild-settings show` (**✏️ Edit numbers**). Each numbered button swaps exactly that pair, and nobody else moves.

Drift is noticed when a team post is built, so it needs a Team Post time on your Gotham events. It only applies when City Hall is picked by **Top power** (see Team rules below).

## The ERT

The **Emergency Response Team** is an extra list on top of everyone's job: they keep their usual place and jump in when something needs fixing during the match. The bot picks the most active cannon players and the strongest City Hall players, by default 8 and 4 (**ERT from Cannons** and **ERT from City Hall** on the **DC Dark Legion** tab of `/guild-settings show`).

`/teams ert` shows the ERT and lets you add or remove people. Once you edit it, you pick the ERT and setup leaves it alone; **↩ Let the bot pick again** hands it back (Premium). On Free you always pick the ERT yourself.

## Team rules (Premium)

`/teams composition` sets how the teams are built, separately for Ultimate and Battle for Gotham (**Copy these rules to…** copies one to the other). Changing the rules needs **Manage settings & permissions**.

**City Hall**, and how many hold it (default 30):

- **Top power**: the strongest players.
- **Power range**: players inside a power band you set.
- **Spread across power**: some strong, some middle, some lower.

**Cannon teams**, 1 to 6 of them (default 3):

- **Balanced**: even total power.
- **Tiered**: Team A strongest, down to the last team.

**Team sizes** can be set per team, for example `25, 25, 20` (`any` for no limit). Extra players go to **Reserves**.

**Cannons each team covers**: by default Cannon Team A covers Cannon 1, B Cannon 2, and so on (six cannons in an Ultimate, four in a Battle for Gotham, so a BfG's Teams E and F support the others). The post shows each team's cannon and its side around City Hall. To change it, **Edit** it on the panel: one line a team, `A: 1, 2 | South Side | a note`. Leave the form blank to go back to the default. A cannon can be covered by more than one team.

Saving a rule moves nobody. The panel shows who a rebuild would move, with **Rebuild teams now** or **Keep current teams**.
